name: Vesmo Elektromotory a.s.
summary: Vesmo is a large, financially sound Czech motor maker: 1,200 staff, EUR 192 M turnover, owner_type group, equity 37.4 %, credit index stable at 173. Its key account manager cannot approve price changes above 2 % without a pricing committee that meets every two weeks, and its sales director says they are reviewing small accounts. We are only 1.2 % of its turnover. Its copper is bought forward until March 2027, its 2027 quotes are flat at current prices, and its delivery and quality figures are slipping while the scorecard is still green.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 % price change; above 2 % the pricing committee (meets every two weeks); the sales director sets account priorities

negotiation_pattern: Opens annual renewals with a moderate ask and settles well below it. Asks were 2.7-4.7 % with settlements of 1.2-1.4 % in the last two rounds; in 2024 it asked -0.9/-0.7 % and settled at -2.6 %. The mean ask is 2.27 % and the mean settlement is 0.0 %. Every settled change stayed within the 2 % band the key account manager can approve alone. For 2027 it has quoted flat prices, but only for as long as its copper cover lasts (until March 2027). It argues from its own cost reality ('market price is not our reality' before March 2027), not from market indices.
wants: Volume and account relevance (it is focusing on customers with volume; our spend is growing)
Price changes inside the 2 % band, so no committee loop is needed
Freedom to reprice after its copper hedge ends in March 2027
Reliable payment (we pay late 83 % of the time)
protects: unit_price below its quoted level (prices sit only about 1.7-1.9 % above our no-margin should-cost; changes above 2 % need the committee)
Price validity beyond March 2027 (it ties validity to its copper cover)

trades.give: Pay strictly on time at 45 days (stop the average 3.1 days late)
trades.get: unit_price held flat for all of calendar year 2027, not just until March 2027
trades.why: Costs us almost nothing, fixes a real irritant, and matches clause 3.1, which fixes prices per calendar year.

trades.give: contract_months up to 24 plus a higher volume_per_year / quota on part:350010 (now 30 %)
trades.get: unit_price -1 to -2 % from 2027-01-01, or flat price fixed through 2027
trades.why: Volume answers its small-account review, and a move of 2 % or less stays within the key account manager's authority.

trades.give: Symmetric copper index_clause with a deadband, starting only after March 2027
trades.get: No list-price increase for 2027; any later change runs only through the index
trades.why: Matches its stated cost reality (hedged until March 2027) and replaces a blanket increase with a transparent mechanism.

trades.give: Rolling 6-12 month forecast for both parts
trades.get: OTD recovery plan toward the 95 % target, a ppm_commitment (e.g. <300) and a higher chargeback_eur_per_complaint
trades.why: OTD is 81.1 % against a 95 % target and ppm rose from 0 to 764; a forecast removes its planning excuse.

arguments.point: Your copper is fixed until March 2027 by your own account, so there is no cost basis for raising 2027 prices. Clause 3.1 fixes prices for each calendar year, so a validity limited to March 2027 does not fit the contract.
Price changes need written notice at least 90 days before year end (about 2026-10-02), and your offer is flat, so 2027 pricing should stay flat for the full year.
We are a growing account, not a shrinking small one: spend went from EUR 1.83 M to 2.06 M to 2.21 M (FY2024 to FY2026).
Performance is drifting: OTD is 81.1 % against the 95 % contractual target, ppm went from 0 to 764 within a year, and one 8D is still open. We expect a recovery plan before discussing anything else.
Part:350010 already has a second source (30 % quota here), so quota can move toward the better performer.

avoid: Hard price-down demands built on should-cost. Confidence is only 5 %, and prices are just +1.7 % / +1.9 % over its own no-margin cost (part:350010 is even 7.7 % below the other plant's cost estimate).
Asks above 2 % in either direction. They trigger the biweekly pricing committee and slow everything down.
Threatening to walk away. We are 1.2 % of its turnover, it is already reviewing small accounts, and part:350012 is 100 % with Vesmo.
Arguing with copper market prices before March 2027. It has explicitly rejected that line.
tone: Businesslike and structured. Frame offers so the key account manager can approve them alone (within 2 %), lead with volume and contract terms, and state quality facts plainly without hostility.
red_flags: Risk of being deprioritized as a small account (doc:20260413-70520-M2)
Price increase risk once the copper hedge ends in March 2027 (doc:20260620-70520-M1)
Delivery reliability worsening: OTD 81.1 % against a 95 % target (sc:70520@2026Q3)
ppm trend rising from 0 to 764, with one open 8D
Contract auto-renews unless terminated with 90 days' notice, which expires around 2026-10-02 (ctr:4600070520#8.1)

evidence.claim: Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval; the committee meets every two weeks.
Copper is bought forward until March 2027; the 2027 quotes are flat with validity tied to that cover.
Sales director is reviewing small accounts and will focus on customers with volume.
Recent asks of 2.7-4.7 % settled at 1.2-1.4 %; the 2024 round settled at -2.6 %.
OTD fell to 81.1 % and ppm rose to 764 against a 95 % OTD target; complaint flat fee is EUR 150.
Prices are about 1.7-1.9 % above its no-margin should-cost (low 5 % confidence).
Contract fixes prices per calendar year with 90-day notice, and auto-extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice.

indicators.credit_index: 173 (12 months ago 173; higher is worse, >300 weak)
price_vs_should_cost_no_margin: part:350012: price 601.27 vs cost:350012 591.2 (its own plant): +1.7 %
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 84.6, ppm 0) → 2026Q1 green (otd 83.0, ppm 401) → 2026Q2 green (otd 84.6, ppm 588) → 2026Q3 green (otd 81.1, ppm 764)
